scope: Owner projection, Alexander predicate transport, and identifiability extensions

sources.title: A general and efficient representation of ancestral recombination graphs
sources.locator: Genome ARGs paragraphs 1/3/4/5; Figure 1; Appendix D paragraph 1; genomic nodes and interval-labelled inheritance
sources.role: Motivation for supplied ownership and possibly compressed pedigree paths

sources.title: Specieslike clusters based on identical ancestor points
sources.role: Exact source definitions, not a source claim of the new projection theorem

sources.title: The existence and abundance of ghost ancestors in biparental populations
sources.role: Prior probabilistic work on genealogical ancestors without genetic contribution; not re-formalized

sources.title: Reconstructing pedigrees: some identifiability questions for a recombination-mutation model
sources.role: Prior model-dependent statistical identifiability; distinguishes distributional recovery from exact finite-data decoding

claims.statement: A supplied edge-sound owner map takes each genomic path to equality or pedigree ancestry.
assumptions: every represented edge is biologically sound for the chosen pedigree
not_claimed: owner map inferred from a bare gARG

claims.statement: An onto map with finite fibres preserves and reflects finiteness of saturated sets.
assumptions: each owner fibre finite; no uniform bound required

claims.statement: IAP and REF agree between an organism candidate S and the saturated rich candidate owner^-1(S).
assumptions: strict ancestry equivalence for every pair of representatives with different owners
not_claimed: sampled finite ARGs satisfy these assumptions
equivalence for arbitrary nonsaturated rich sets

claims.statement: Convexity pulls back under sound paths; it is equivalent under surjectivity, target acyclicity, and ancestry equivalence away from fibres.
assumptions: surjectivity, target acyclicity and ancestry reflection for descent

claims.statement: Specieslike status descends, and becomes equivalent on saturated sets if each owner fibre is weakly connected internally.
assumptions: connected owner fibres for reverse direction

claims.statement: Pedigree maximality is equivalent to maximality among saturated rich candidates; unrestricted rich maximality of a saturated set descends.
assumptions: all comparison sets included in the explicitly stated candidate family
not_claimed: target maximality implies unrestricted rich maximality

claims.statement: A common ancestor in a saturated rich candidate projects to a pedigree common ancestor.
not_claimed: converse without a within-fibre ancestor condition

claims.statement: IAP is unchanged when every source member has only finitely many discrepant descendant answers inside the candidate.
assumptions: row-wise finite symmetric differences of ancestry-path predicates
not_claimed: these error bounds hold in empirical ARG inference

claims.statement: The same infinite connected rich history and fixed identity owner map have two sound biosphere interpretations with opposite IAP.
assumptions: abstract ancestry graphs with natural birthdates
not_claimed: same observation distribution in a specified diploid inheritance law

claims.statement: No deterministic summary of finite gARG data permits an exact universal whole-specieslike decoder over the abstract completion class.
assumptions: topology-compatible abstract completions as already defined in the repository
not_claimed: impossibility of probabilistic inference under demographic assumptions

claims.statement: A specified biparental/recombination law admits ancestors of all present organisms that leave no present genetic material.
Under explicit recombination/mutation models and parameter restrictions, dependence across sites identifies some pedigree invariants.
